opts: The 40-50% rise in cardiac output far exceeds tissue oxygen extraction
Fetal tissues consume no oxygen at all throughout the pregnancy
Maternal hemoglobin loses its ability to bind and carry oxygen
Maternal systemic vascular resistance rises during pregnancy
exp: Oxygen consumption rises 20% but the A-V gradient falls because the disproportionate 40-50% surge in maternal cardiac output delivers oxygen far in excess of tissue extraction.

opts: ROP then DOP then LOP; android pelvis, then a deflexed head
LOP then DOP then ROP; anthropoid pelvis, then macrosomia
DOP then ROP then LOP; platypelloid pelvis, then a deflexed head
LOP then ROP then DOP; gynaecoid pelvis, then a deflexed head
exp: The commonest OP positions in order are ROP, DOP and LOP; the causes are the android pelvis (commonest, the head occupying the posterior part because of the extra space) and then a deflexed head.

opts: Insulin to control blood sugar and anti-D prophylaxis
Low-dose aspirin for prevention and strict bed rest
Cervical cerclage and vaginal progesterone support
Magnesium sulfate for seizures and antihypertensives for BP
exp: After airway and safety measures, eclampsia is treated with two pillars: magnesium sulfate for seizures and antihypertensives for blood pressure.

opts: Intrahepatic cholestasis and acute fatty liver of pregnancy
Cirrhosis and acute hepatitis E infection in pregnancy
Gilbert syndrome and Dubin-Johnson syndrome in pregnancy
Budd-Chiari syndrome and portal vein thrombosis in pregnancy
exp: Maternal complications of twin pregnancy include pronounced haemodynamic changes, increased placental size, polyhydramnios, and the liver conditions intrahepatic cholestasis and acute fatty liver of pregnancy.

opts: B-Lynch or Brace, then Hayman, Cho square, Pereira, Gunshella
McDonald, then Shirodkar, then the Wurm modification
O'Leary, then the Burch procedure, then Kelly plication
Halsted stitch, then the Lembert stitch, then the Connell stitch
exp: Compression sutures for PPH are B-Lynch or Brace (commonest first), then Hayman, the Cho square sutures, Pereira and Gunshella.

opts: 110 to 160 beats per minute
120 to 180 beats per minute
90 to 130 beats per minute
100 to 140 beats per minute
exp: The normal physiological baseline fetal heart rate on CTG is 110 to 160 bpm, evaluated over a minimum 10-minute window.

opts: 38 weeks; 36 weeks; 32-34 weeks by caesarean after corticosteroids
40 weeks; 38 weeks; 36 weeks by caesarean after corticosteroids
36 weeks; 34 weeks; 32 weeks by caesarean after corticosteroids
37 weeks for all three, by caesarean after corticosteroids
exp: Delivery timing is 38 weeks for DCDA twins, 36 weeks for MCDA twins, and 32-34 weeks by caesarean after corticosteroids for MCMA twins.

opts: Cervical repair and suction evacuation; contraindicated in labour (fetal bradycardia)
Instrumental delivery and perineal repair; contraindicated in labour (bradycardia)
Cervical repair and suction evacuation; contraindicated in hypertension
Caesarean section and suturing; contraindicated in multiple pregnancy
exp: Paracervical block is used for repair of the cervix and for suction and evacuation, but is contraindicated in labour because it causes fetal bradycardia.

opts: Pregnancy contraindicated; mortality up to 30-50%, so termination is advised
Pregnancy is safe with routine outpatient visits; mortality under 1%
Caesarean delivery must be performed at 28 weeks; mortality 5-10%
Only oral iron therapy is needed; no excess maternal mortality
exp: In modified WHO class IV, pregnancy is strictly contraindicated, maternal mortality is extremely high (up to 30-50%), and termination is advised if conception occurs.

opts: They chelate calcium in fetal bones and teeth, causing discoloration and enamel hypoplasia
They cause Gray baby syndrome from impaired hepatic conjugation in the fetus
They cause congenital deafness from direct damage to the eighth cranial nerve
They trigger fetal aplastic anaemia through direct bone-marrow suppression
exp: After the 15th week tetracyclines chelate with calcium in fetal bones and teeth, causing permanent yellowish-brown discoloration, enamel hypoplasia and inhibition of bone growth.

opts: Their nadir follows the contraction peak, reflecting uteroplacental insufficiency
They indicate fetal head compression against the pelvic floor and skull
They reflect rapid cord prolapse through the cervix with cord compression
They are caused by maternal sleep and the resulting reduced placental flow
exp: Late decelerations are the most ominous pattern because the nadir occurs after the peak of the contraction, reflecting uteroplacental insufficiency and fetal myocardial hypoxia.

opts: Stop warfarin, deliver by caesarean, and give vitamin K to mother and neonate
Allow spontaneous vaginal delivery, shortened by vacuum extraction
Administer high-dose intravenous aspirin and continue warfarin
Discharge the patient until the warfarin has washed out completely
exp: With a mechanical valve on warfarin in active labour, stop warfarin, perform caesarean delivery and give vitamin K to both mother and neonate to avoid fetal intracranial hemorrhage.

opts: Head engaged: ARM, wait 30 minutes, then oxytocin; not engaged: oxytocin then ARM
Head engaged: oxytocin, wait 30 minutes, then ARM; not engaged: ARM then oxytocin
Head engaged: ARM alone, no oxytocin; not engaged: oxytocin alone, no ARM
Both engaged and not engaged: simultaneous ARM and oxytocin together
exp: With the head engaged, augment by ARM, wait 30 minutes, then oxytocin; with the head not engaged, give oxytocin followed by ARM, since ARM first raises the risk of cord prolapse.

opts: Non-stress test for acute oxygenation, plus amniotic fluid assessment for chronic function
Fetal breathing movements for tone, plus umbilical artery Doppler velocimetry
Fetal tone and body movement, plus maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein
Cardiotocography tracing, plus fetal scalp blood pH estimation
exp: The modified biophysical profile combines the non-stress test, reflecting acute oxygenation, with amniotic fluid assessment / single deepest pocket, reflecting chronic placental function.

opts: Low forceps: downward and backward, then downward, then downward and forward
Outlet forceps in lithotomy: downward, then downward and forward
Low forceps in the supine position: upward, then forward throughout
Outlet forceps in left lateral position: forward only throughout the pull
exp: Pull is directed in lithotomy with the operator's hand on the maternal abdomen; low forceps pull downward and backward, then downward, then downward and forward, while outlet forceps pull downward then downward and forward.

opts: Caesarean at 32-34 weeks after completing a steroid course
Vaginal delivery at 38 weeks after completing a steroid course
Fetal reduction at 12 weeks, then delivery at 38 weeks
Serial amnioreduction, then delivery at 34 completed weeks
exp: Conjoined twins are managed by caesarean section between 32 and 34 weeks after completing the steroid course.

opts: PGF2α; gold standard for PPH; 250 mcg IM every 15-40 min, max 8 doses; diarrhoea
PGE2; first-line alternative; 500 mcg by slow IV injection; pyrexia
PGE1; second-line agent; 1 mg IM repeated four-hourly; hypertension
PGI2; adjunct only; 100 mcg subcutaneously six-hourly; flushing
exp: Carboprost (Hemabate) is PGF2α, the gold standard for PPH management, given as 250 mcg IM every 15-40 minutes to a maximum of 8 doses (2 mg); diarrhoea is the classic side effect.

opts: Packed red cell transfusion with IV furosemide, at any gestational age
Double-dose oral iron therapy continued for a full month
Intravenous iron sucrose 200 mg given daily for a week
Immediate termination of pregnancy after stabilisation
exp: With very severe symptomatic anemia and Hb under 5 g/dL at 24 weeks, the immediate treatment is packed red blood cell transfusion with IV furosemide, irrespective of gestational age.

opts: Diet-controlled gestational diabetes at any gestation
Eclampsia, impending eclampsia, HELLP, fetal distress or abruption
Mild pre-eclampsia alone presenting before 28 weeks
Chronic hypertension alone presenting before 20 weeks
exp: In the p399 table, immediate termination irrespective of gestational age is required for eclampsia, impending eclampsia, HELLP, fetal distress or abruption.

opts: Loss of the normal retroplacental hypoechoic area (decidua basalis)
Gain of a new retroplacental cystic lesion behind the placenta
Marked thickening of the amnion over the placental surface
Absent fetal breathing movements on a 30-minute scan
exp: Besides disruption of the continuous white line, PAS shows loss of the normal retroplacental hypoechoic area (the decidua basalis).

opts: Outlet forceps; short and light; total length 27.5 cm, shank 2.5 cm
Long rotational forceps; total length 35 cm, sliding lock
Forceps for the aftercoming head; total length 27.5 cm
Solid-bladed forceps; short and light, shank 2.5 cm
exp: Wrigley forceps are outlet forceps, short and light, with a total length of 27.5 cm and a shank of 2.5 cm.

opts: Hartmann sign, also called the placental sign
Hegar sign of lower-segment softening
Chadwick sign of bluish discoloration
Palmer sign of regular uterine pulsation
exp: Slight painless spotting around cycle day 20-22 from blastocyst burrowing into the endometrium is the Hartmann sign (placental sign).

opts: A rising pulse with falling BP and severe abdominal pain
Normal vital signs with no abdominal pain at all
Only mild palmar itching with a stable pulse
Fetal macrosomia noted on the scan before the procedure
exp: Karman-cannula perforation is suggested by a raised pulse with falling BP or shock and severe abdominal pain.

opts: Cut: pubococcygeus, transverse perinei, bulbospongiosus; not cut: anal sphincter
Cut: ischiocavernosus, external anal sphincter; not cut: bulbospongiosus
Cut: obturator internus and ischiocavernosus; not cut: pubococcygeus
Cut: external anal sphincter and ischiocavernosus; not cut: transverse perinei
exp: An episiotomy cuts pubococcygeus and the deep and superficial transverse perinei and bulbospongiosus, but not the ischiocavernosus, ischiococcygeus, obturator or anal sphincter.

opts: Serum bile acids and HbA1c estimation
DIPSI testing and fetal echocardiography
APLA antibody testing and parental karyotyping
TORCH screening and VDRL serology
exp: After recurrent losses the source plan routinely includes the etiologic tests APLA antibody testing and parental karyotyping.

opts: Urine pregnancy test, positive in about 99% because of beta-hCG
Middle cerebral artery Doppler velocimetry of the fetus
Indirect Coombs test performed on maternal serum
Hysterosalpingography to outline the uterine cavity
exp: In amenorrhea with P/V bleeding and abdominal pain, the first investigation for ectopic pregnancy is a urine pregnancy test, positive in about 99% because of beta-hCG.

opts: 42 weeks or more, that is 294 days or more
40 weeks or more, that is 280 days or more
41 weeks or more, that is 287 days or more
37 weeks or more, that is 259 days or more
exp: Post-term pregnancy is defined as 42 weeks or more (294 days or more).

opts: 16 to 18 weeks of gestation, acceptable 15 to 20 weeks
11 to 13 weeks and 6 days of gestation, acceptable 10 to 14
24 to 28 weeks of gestation, acceptable 22 to 30 weeks
6 to 8 weeks of gestation, acceptable 5 to 9 weeks
exp: The optimal window for maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein screening is 16 to 18 weeks, with 15 to 20 weeks acceptable.

opts: Under 1 cm/hr dilatation; descent under 1 cm/hr in primigravida or 2 cm/hr in multipara
Under 2 cm/hr dilatation; descent under 1 cm/hr in both primigravida and multipara
Under 1 cm/hr dilatation; descent under 2 cm/hr in primigravida or 1 cm/hr in multipara
No progress in dilatation for 2 hours; no descent of the head for 1 hour
exp: Protracted active phase is cervical dilatation under 1 cm/hr, or descent of the head under 1 cm/hr in a primigravida or under 2 cm/hr in a multigravida.

opts: 2 ova fertilized by 2 different sperms; 1 ovum fertilized by 1 sperm then dividing into 2
1 ovum fertilized by 2 different sperms; 2 separate ova fusing together
Both twins arise from one zygote that splits after fertilisation
Both twins arise from two zygotes that implant separately
exp: Dizygotic twins form when 2 ova are fertilized by 2 different sperms, whereas monozygotic twins form when a single ovum fertilized by a single sperm divides into 2.

opts: Dexamethasone 4 doses of 6 mg IM 12-hourly; betamethasone 2 doses of 12 mg 24-hourly
Dexamethasone 2 doses of 12 mg 24-hourly; betamethasone 4 doses of 6 mg 12-hourly
Dexamethasone 4 doses of 6 mg IM 12-hourly; betamethasone 4 doses of 6 mg 12-hourly
Both given as a single dose of 12 mg IM, repeated if delivery is delayed
exp: Dexamethasone (DOC in India) is 4 doses of 6 mg IM 12 hours apart; betamethasone (DOC worldwide) is 2 doses of 12 mg 24 hours apart and carries a slightly higher fetal hypoglycaemia risk.

opts: The bladder-serosa interface, appearing hypervascular on Doppler
The umbilical cord insertion into the placental mass
The cervix and the adjacent lower uterine segment
The veins of the broad ligament and ovarian plexus
exp: Bridging vessels in PAS are seen between the placenta and the bladder-serosa interface, appearing hypervascular on Doppler.

opts: Schultze: central separation, shiny fetal surface first; Duncan: peripheral separation, dull maternal surface first
Schultze: peripheral separation, dull maternal surface first; Duncan: central separation, shiny fetal surface first
Schultze: continuous bleeding from the start; Duncan: bleeding appears only after expulsion
Schultze: peripheral detachment with no retroplacental clot; Duncan: central detachment with a large clot
exp: Schultze (80%) separates centrally, the shiny fetal surface is expelled first and bleeding is seen only after expulsion; Duncan (20%) separates peripherally, the dull maternal surface is expelled first and bleeding is continuous.

opts: The concern is gross anomalies, whereas karyotyping detects chromosomal abnormalities
Karyotyping detects maternal diabetes and no other fetal condition
Karyotyping cannot technically be performed at all during pregnancy
Karyotyping is the definitive diagnostic test for a fetal VSD
exp: Routine karyotyping is not used for diabetic congenital-anomaly assessment because the concern is gross congenital anomalies, whereas karyotyping detects chromosomal abnormalities.

opts: Stable vitals, no active bleeding, under 37 weeks, reactive CTG, no major anomaly
Unstable vitals with active bleeding, under 37 weeks, non-reactive CTG
Stable vitals, no active bleeding, under 37 weeks, fetal distress on CTG
A gross congenital anomaly in a non-viable fetus, with stable vitals
exp: Expectant management of bleeding previa requires all of: stable vitals, absent active bleeding, under 37 weeks, reactive CTG, and no or only a minor anomaly.

opts: Perineal massage, warm towel, support the perineum, flex then extend the head
Routine episiotomy, fundal pressure, and early maternal pushing efforts
Lithotomy position, the Kristeller manoeuvre, and perineal shaving
Vacuum extraction, perineal shaving, and routine episiotomy in all
exp: WHO recommends perineal massage, a warm towel at the perineum, supporting the perineum with the hand, and flexing the head initially then extending it for delivery.

opts: Macrosomia, post-term pregnancy, and malpresentation such as breech
Twin pregnancy, polyhydramnios, and a previous caesarean section
A previous vaginal delivery and a low transverse uterine scar
Maternal age above 30 and a short interdelivery interval
exp: Relative contraindications where repeat caesarean is preferred are macrosomia, post-term pregnancy and malpresentation such as breech.

opts: 1st and 2nd degree in the labour room under local anaesthesia; 3rd and 4th in theatre
1st and 2nd degree in the labour room under local anaesthesia; all degrees in theatre
1st and 2nd degree at the bedside without anaesthesia; 3rd and 4th in theatre
All degrees are repaired in theatre under general or spinal anaesthesia
exp: First and second degree tears are repaired in the labour room under local anaesthesia like an episiotomy; third and fourth degree tears are repaired in the OT under general or spinal anaesthesia, using Vicryl for both.

opts: Turner syndrome (45,X monosomy)
Triploidy with a 69,XXX karyotype
Balanced chromosomal translocation
Trisomy 16 with a full autosomal trisomy
exp: The most common chromosomal abnormality in recurrent abortion is a balanced chromosomal translocation.

opts: At least 2 accelerations of 15 bpm for 15 seconds in 20 minutes, with variability
No accelerations at all, with a flat baseline over the full 20 minutes
One continuous acceleration lasting longer than 10 minutes throughout
Early decelerations with every contraction, with normal variability
exp: A reactive non-stress test over 20 minutes at term shows at least 2 qualifying accelerations of 15 bpm for 15 seconds, with normal baseline and moderate variability.

opts: Gestational sac in the ampulla with a visible yolk sac
No uteroperitoneal fistula, normal tubes and ovaries, peritoneal attachment
An open internal os with the gestational sac lying in the endocervix
A gestational sac in the ovary with ovarian tissue in its wall
exp: Studdiford criteria for primary abdominal ectopic pregnancy are: no uteroperitoneal fistula, normal tubes and ovaries, and a pregnancy attached to the peritoneum.

opts: Reposition last what prolapsed first; do not separate the placenta
Remove the placenta first, then replace the fundus into the pelvis
Push the cervix upwards first, then replace the uterine fundus
Apply steady traction to the cord until the uterus is fully delivered
exp: Johnson's method: the part that prolapsed first is repositioned last, and the placenta is not separated, since separation increases haemorrhage.

opts: Ripening: sweeping, mechanical, prostaglandins; IOL: mechanical, PG, oxytocin; augmentation: oxytocin, ARM
Ripening: oxytocin and ARM; IOL: sweeping of membranes; augmentation: prostaglandins
Ripening: prostaglandins only; IOL: ARM only; augmentation: oxytocin only
Ripening: mechanical methods; IOL: sweeping only; augmentation: prostaglandins
exp: Cervical ripening uses sweeping of membranes, mechanical methods and prostaglandins; induction of labour uses mechanical methods, prostaglandins and oxytocin; augmentation uses oxytocin and ARM.

opts: 10 to 14 weeks of gestation, ideally 11 to 13 weeks and 6 days
15 to 20 weeks of gestation, ideally 16 to 18 completed weeks
6 to 8 weeks of gestation, ideally at 7 completed weeks
18 to 22 weeks of gestation, ideally at 20 completed weeks
exp: The optimal window for chorionic villus sampling is 10 to 14 weeks, ideally 11 to 13 weeks and 6 days.
